title: Adjunction triangles induce coherent mapping-space equivalences
statement:
Use quasicategories, coherent functors, transformations, full subcategories and mapping spaces from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and canonical mapping-space composition from [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition]. Work in a fixed containing universe. Let $F:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ and $G:\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$ be coherent functors and let $\eta:\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal C}\to GF$, $\epsilon:FG\to\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal D}$ be coherent transformations with homotopies $G\epsilon\circ\eta G\simeq1_G$ and $\epsilon F\circ F\eta\simeq1_F$ in their functor quasicategories. Then the adjunct maps
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D}(Fx,d)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(x,Gd),\qquad v\longmapsto G(v)\circ\eta_x$$
are equivalences of spaces, coherently natural in $x\in\mathcal C$ and $d\in\mathcal D$. Their inverse homotopy classes are represented by $u\longmapsto\epsilon_d\circ F(u)$. Naturality here is an equivalence of the associated space-valued mapping bifunctors on $\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}}\times\mathcal D$, including their simplicial coherence.

source.place: Kerodon 02F1, Proposition 6.2.1.17 and its test-Kan-complex proof; the dual counit formula and coherent parameter dependence use Definition 6.2.1.1 (02EK) and the mapping-space composition of Construction 4.6.8.9 (01PF). Read online 2026-10-17, not archived. Kerodon identifiers, not Stacks tags.

proof.text: Enlarge the universe of spaces so that $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ and their mapping spaces are small there; this uses no local-smallness hypothesis beyond fitting in the containing universe. Put $B=\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}}\times\mathcal D$, $P(x,d)=H_{\mathcal D}(Fx,d)$ and $Q(x,d)=H_{\mathcal C}(x,Gd)$, using [lem-coef-infinity-hom-bifunctor-functoriality] and [def-coef-infinity-category-of-spaces]. The comparison for $G$, restricted along $(F,\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal D})$, gives $P\to H_{\mathcal C}(GF(-),G(-))$. Apply $H_{\mathcal C}$ contravariantly to the actual transformation $\eta:\mathrm{id}\to GF$, and covariantly to $Gd$, to obtain $H_{\mathcal C}(GF(-),G(-))\to Q$. Their composite is a coherent transformation $\Phi:P\to Q$ with component $v\mapsto G(v)\eta_x$. Similarly the comparison for $F$ gives $Q\to H_{\mathcal D}(F(-),FG(-))$ and covariant application of $H_{\mathcal D}$ to $\epsilon:FG\to\mathrm{id}$ gives a coherent transformation $\Psi:Q\to P$ with component $u\mapsto\epsilon_dF(u)$. Contravariance reverses the direction of $\eta$ in the first construction. The target $\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}$ is a quasicategory by [lem-coef-kan-coherent-nerve-quasicategory], so $\operatorname{Fun}(B,\mathcal S_{\mathcal U})$ is a quasicategory and composites of these transformations exist by inner $2$-horn filling in it, supplied by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]; the canonical composition and identification of their component classes are [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition]. Thus their naturality is already on all simplices of $B$, before invertibility is proved.

Here is the mapping-space naturality homotopy used in both calculations, rather than only a calculation on edges. For an actual transformation $\alpha:A\to A'$ of functors $\mathcal E\to\mathcal V$, view it, by [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], as the simplicial functor $\widetilde\alpha:\mathcal E\times\Delta^1\to\mathcal V$. Fix $a,b\in\mathcal E$. In $\mathcal E\times\Delta^1$, a variable arrow $v:a\to b$ has two factorizations from $(a,0)$ to $(b,1)$: first $v$ at endpoint $0$ and then the interval edge at $b$, or first the interval edge at $a$ and then $v$ at endpoint $1$. The right-pinched mapping space between these mixed endpoints is degreewise $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(a,b)$: the interval coordinate of each defining simplex is forced to be $0$ on its initial face and $1$ at its last vertex. Both composition maps identify with the identity on this space, by the product formula and unitality. Apply [lem-cbc-simplicial-composition-spine], whose coherent face/degeneracy operations are natural in simplicial functors, to $\widetilde\alpha$. The images of the two factorizations are therefore homotopic as maps of the entire Kan space:
$$\alpha_b\circ A(v)\simeq A'(v)\circ\alpha_a.$$
This supplies the homotopy for arbitrary higher simplices $v$, with no invertibility assumption on $v$ or $\alpha$. Composition on the right-pinched models and its functoriality are identified by [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition] and [lem-coef-infinity-hom-bifunctor-functoriality].

source.place: 02F1 uses functor-category adjuncts; explicit parameter-prism expansion of naturality, using 01PF spine composition

proof.text:
For $v\in\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D}(Fx,d)$, use functoriality and associativity of composition from [lem-coef-infinity-hom-bifunctor-functoriality] and [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition], and apply the naturality homotopy of step 2 to $\alpha=\epsilon$, $A=FG$, $A'=\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal D}$, $a=Fx$, $b=d$. This gives homotopies of maps of the whole mapping space
$$\Psi_{x,d}\Phi_{x,d}(v)\simeq\epsilon_d\circ FG(v)\circ F(\eta_x)\simeq v\circ\epsilon_{Fx}\circ F(\eta_x)\simeq v.$$
The last homotopy is evaluation at $x$ of the assumed triangle $\epsilon F\circ F\eta\simeq1_F$, followed by composition with the variable $v$ and the unit homotopy. Evaluation restricts the given functor-quasicategory homotopy to the selected vertex by [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]; hence this is a homotopy of maps, not merely equality of components.

For $u\in\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(x,Gd)$, use the same functoriality and associativity statements, and apply step 2 to $\alpha=\eta$, $A=\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal C}$, $A'=GF$, $a=x$, $b=Gd$. Then
$$\Phi_{x,d}\Psi_{x,d}(u)\simeq G(\epsilon_d)\circ GF(u)\circ\eta_x\simeq G(\epsilon_d)\circ\eta_{Gd}\circ u\simeq u.$$
The final homotopy is the assumed triangle $G\epsilon\circ\eta G\simeq1_G$ evaluated at $d$, followed by composition and unitality. These are again homotopies of maps of the full mapping spaces, using [lem-coef-infinity-hom-bifunctor-functoriality], [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition] and evaluation in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Neither triangle homotopy was inferred from the other.

The homotopies in steps 3 and 4 make $\Psi_{x,d}$ a simplicial homotopy inverse of $\Phi_{x,d}$. By [lem-cbc-simplicial-homotopy-equivalence-weak], each component $\Phi_{x,d}$ is a weak homotopy equivalence, including empty mapping spaces. Apply [lem-coef-kan-coherent-nerve-inverse-equivalence] to the two maps of Kan complexes: it supplies actual inverse-triangle $2$-simplices in $\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}=N_{\mathrm{hc}}(\mathbf{Kan}_{\mathcal U})$, so each component is an equivalence edge. Step 1 already constructed $\Phi$ as an edge of $\operatorname{Fun}(B,\mathcal S_{\mathcal U})$. The target is a quasicategory by [lem-coef-kan-coherent-nerve-quasicategory], so [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-equivalences] upgrades this coherent transformation to an equivalence. Its inverse component homotopy classes are represented by $u\mapsto\epsilon_d\circ F(u)$ by steps 1 and 4, proving the stated coherent bifunctor equivalence.
